text:
Alex: After the 3-hour outage yesterday I sketched a small pilot for a runbook-driven remediation bot that can: automatically suggest the top 1-2 low-risk mitigations, surface a short customer-impact assessment, and capture an on-call handoff note if it needs escalation. thinking: pilot on staging first, then a canary on prod for minor incidents only.

Maria: big +1. we keep doing manual triage for the same set of issues (LB spikes, 504 cascades, K8s pod flaps). if we can automate the first mitigation step and unify the handoff note, postmortem scheduling becomes way easier.

Jon: curious about integrations — do you mean incident-bot would POST a payload to remediate-bot and remediate-bot would reply with suggested actions? if so we should ensure each suggestion carries a confidence + quick rollback note. also needs to create an action item in the PM dashboard when something is applied.

Sara: safety guardrails are 🔑. no autop-run for anything that touches DB or infra changes. allow two modes: "suggest-only" (default) and "apply-with-approval" (for ops leads). we also should surface expected user-visible impact and a short how-we-detected line for the postmortem.

ops-bot: Incident 2076543209 referenced: 504 spike (service: inference-proxy). Notifying #eng-oncall thread. :rotating_light:

Alex: exactly — pilot rules:
- scope: inference-proxy 504s, autoscaler thrash, and p95 latency regressions that match known fingerprints
- mode: suggest-only on first 2 weeks, then canary apply-with-approval on a handful of safe mitigations (route traffic away, restart replica).
- output: 1) short mitigation suggestion, 2) customer-impact bullet (one-liner), 3) handoff note template, 4) create PM calendar invite for postmortem if impact >= medium.

Sam: UI/UX note — on-call needs a single-button flow in Slack: "Propose mitigation" -> bot posts suggestions -> oncall clicks "Apply" or "Dismiss". clicking Apply should open a small confirm modal with a prefilled rollback. keeps noise down.

Maria: here's a draft of the handoff template the bot would save into the action tracker (short fields only):
```
- Incident ID: <id>
- Time window: <start> - <end>
- Customer impact: <none/minor/medium/major>
- Mitigation attempted: <text>
- Owner: <name>
- Follow-ups: <short bullets + due dates>
```
Make sure the "Customer impact" map ties to auto calendar scheduling (medium+ => schedule postmortem).

Jon: example webhook payload we can send to remediate-bot (sketch):
```json
{
  "incident_id": "2076543209",
  "fingerprint": "proxy-504-lb-surge-v1",
  "recent_logs": ["..."],
  "metrics": {"p99_latency": 1200, "error_rate": 0.08}
}
```
remediate-bot: Received payload for incident 2076543209. Running policy match: proxy-504-lb-surge-v1 -> suggested mitigations: ["scale-up-proxy-pool (safety: low)", "route-troublesome-ips (safety: medium)", "restart-proxy-replica (safety: low)"]

Sara: two follow-ups from me:
1) we need an allowlist for auto-suggested mitigations (ops leads maintain)
2) add a flag so that any mitigation with safety >= medium requires an explicit ops lead approval button (not just any oncall).

Alex: agreed. action items I propose: 
- Alex: draft pilot runbook and interception rules by EOD Friday (2076620000).
- Maria: wire the handoff template to action-tracker API (small PR) — next week.
- Jon: start a webhook stub and a mock responder so we can demo in staging.
- Sara: put together safety allowlist and approval flow docs.
- Sam: prototype the Slack modal for Apply/Approve buttons and confirm flow.

Maria: also proposing that the bot auto-create a postmortem calendar event if "Customer impact" is medium/major and assign provisional facilitator from rotation. reduces friction.

Alex: love that. ok can we all aim to have a 15m async demo in #eng-oncall next Tuesday? drop quick status updates here. :thumbsup:

Sam: I'll put a placeholder calendar invite and link the staging demo channel.

Jon: started the repo stub: https://github.com/redwood/remediate-bot (WIP). I'll post PRs as I go.

Sara: noted — I'll add the approval flow doc to the ops runbooks repo and ping rotation owners for the allowlist.

Alex: thanks team. small ask: when you push updates, prefix commit messages with "remediate-pilot:" so we can grep later. we'll iterate fast and keep the apply-button gated.
